title: Position: Let’s Strengthen Verifiability if We Can’t Enforce Reproducibility
claim: Across major venues, code and weight sharing are stagnating or declining while acknowledgment of prior repositories keeps growing.
layout: 3 stacked line-plot panels, shared year axis, one shared bottom legend
description: Three vertically stacked line charts share an x-axis of years 2021 to 2025 and a y-axis labeled Ratio (%). Panel (a) shows the share of accepted papers with train or test code, panel (b) the share with available model weights, and panel (c) the share acknowledging other repositories. Each panel has six series: CVPR (blue circles), ICCV (orange squares), ICLR (green triangles), ICML (pink diamonds), NeurIPS (yellow pentagons) and a dashed light-blue 'All' average. Panel titles sit above each plot in serif text. One legend runs along the bottom. In (a) and (b) most lines are flat or fall slightly after 2023. In (c) nearly all lines rise. The eye goes to the dashed 'All' line and the overall trend directions. The palette is colorblind-friendly.
caption: Proportion of accepted papers at CVPR, ICCV, ICLR, ICML and NeurIPS 2021–2025 that publicly (a) share train or test code [reducing], (b) provide pretrained model weights [reducing], or (c) acknowledge previous repositories [growing].
abstract: In the field of Machine Learning, many papers contain empirical results supporting claimed statements or illustrating the performance of a proposed method. However, most practitioners know that (1) results are generally hard to reproduce, and increasingly so, (2) code is not often available to do so, and (3) it hinders the development of research. In this position paper, we analyze and quantify these issues, and make concrete proposals to improve result checkability, if not reproducibility. Code and supporting materials are available at https://github.com/giddyyupp/position-enforce-verifiability.
